stem: Find the value of 3/4 ÷ 6.
working: Dividing by 6 is the same as multiplying by 1/6 (Keep, Change, Flip).
3/24 = 1/8 in its simplest form (divide the top and bottom by 3).

distractors.1: Multiplied by 6 instead of dividing. Sharing 3/4 into 6 parts makes each part smaller, not bigger.
distractors.3: Added 6 to the denominator. To divide by 6, multiply by 1/6 instead.
distractors.4: Worked out 6 ÷ 3/4 instead. The order of a division matters: here 3/4 is being shared into 6 parts.

hints: Dividing by a whole number is the same as multiplying by one over that number.
Write 6 as 6/1, flip it, multiply, then simplify your answer.

stem: Hakim had some marbles. He gave 1/3 of them to his brother and 3/5 of the remainder to his cousin. He had 24 marbles left. How many marbles did Hakim have at first?
working: After giving away 1/3, he had 2/3 of his marbles left (the remainder).
The cousin got 3/5 of the remainder, so 2/5 of the remainder was left.
2/5 of the remainder = 24 → 1/5 of the remainder = 12 → the remainder = 60 marbles.
The remainder is 2/3 of all the marbles: 2/3 = 60 → 1/3 = 30 → at first = 90 marbles.
hints: After he gives 1/3 away, draw a new bar for the remainder and cut it into 5 equal parts.
The 24 marbles left are 2 of those 5 parts. Work back to the remainder first, then to the whole.

stem: At a fruit stall, 2/5 of the fruits are apples and 1/3 of the fruits are pears. The rest are 48 oranges. How many more apples than pears are there?
working: Use 15 units for all the fruits (15 is the LCM of 5 and 3).
Apples = 2/5 × 15 = 6 units. Pears = 1/3 × 15 = 5 units. Oranges = 15 − 6 − 5 = 4 units.
Apples − pears = 6 units − 5 units = 1 unit = 12. Check: 72 apples, 60 pears and 48 oranges make 180 fruits ✓

distractors.1: That is the number of apples. The question asks how many MORE apples than pears.
distractors.2: That is the total number of fruits at the stall.
distractors.4: That is the number of pears. Compare it with the number of apples.

hints: Choose a number of units for all the fruits that both 5 and 3 divide into.
Find how many units the oranges are, then how many units more apples there are than pears.

stem: To make one tray of muffins, Nurul mixes flour and sugar in the ratio 5 : 2. Each tray uses 250 g of flour. She has 2 kg of flour and 900 g of sugar. What is the greatest number of trays of muffins she can make?
working: Flour : sugar = 5 : 2, and 5 units = 250 g → 1 unit = 50 g. Each tray needs 2 × 50 g = 100 g of sugar.
The flour is enough for 2000 g ÷ 250 g = 8 trays.
The sugar is enough for 900 g ÷ 100 g = 9 trays.
The flour runs out first, so the greatest number she can make is 8 trays.

distractors.2: That is how many trays the sugar alone allows. Check the flour too: the ingredient that runs out first decides.
distractors.3: Used 250 g of sugar for each tray. The 250 g is the flour; use the ratio to find the sugar for one tray.
distractors.4: Added the flour and the sugar together. Each ingredient has to be checked on its own.

hints: How much sugar does ONE tray need? Use the ratio and the 250 g of flour.
Work out how many trays the flour allows and how many trays the sugar allows. Which runs out first?

stem:

| Duration | Charge |
| --- | --- |
| First hour | $2.50 |
| Every additional 30 min or part thereof | $1.20 |

Mrs Lim parked her car from 9.40 a.m. to 1.15 p.m. How much did she pay?
working: Time parked: 9.40 a.m. to 1.15 p.m. = 3 h 35 min.
After the first hour: 3 h 35 min − 1 h = 2 h 35 min = 155 min.
155 min ÷ 30 min = 5 full blocks with 5 min left over. 'Part thereof' means the 5 min is charged as 1 more block → 6 blocks.
hints: Find how long the car was parked, then take away the first hour.

stem: Tank A is 50 cm long and 30 cm wide. It contains water to a height of 36 cm. Tank B is empty, and its base is 40 cm long and 30 cm wide. Some water is poured from Tank A into Tank B until the water in both tanks is at the same height. No water overflows. Find the height of the water in each tank.
working: Water is only moved, so the total stays the same: 50 × 30 × 36 = 54 000 cm³.
Base areas: Tank A = 50 × 30 = 1500 cm², Tank B = 40 × 30 = 1200 cm². Together = 2700 cm².
Same height in both: height = 54 000 ÷ 2700 = 20 cm.
Check: Tank A holds 1500 × 20 = 30 000 cm³ and Tank B holds 1200 × 20 = 24 000 cm³; 30 000 + 24 000 = 54 000 ✓
hints: Water is only moved, not lost. Find the total volume of water first.
When the heights are equal, the water stands on both bases together. Add the two base areas.

stem: Lines AB and CD are parallel. A straight line cuts AB at G and CD at H. Points A and C are on the same side of line GH. ∠AGH = 72°. Find ∠GHC.

stem: Which shape has exactly 2 lines of symmetry?

A square has 4 lines of symmetry, an equilateral triangle has 3 and an isosceles trapezium has 1.

distractors.1: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: 2 through the middles of the sides and 2 along the diagonals.
distractors.3: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
distractors.4: An isosceles trapezium has only 1 line of symmetry, through the middles of its two parallel sides.

hints: Imagine folding each shape so that the two halves match exactly. How many different folds work?

stem: Pie chart X shows the favourite fruits of the pupils in Class A. Pie chart Y shows the favourite fruits of the pupils in Class B. In pie chart X, 40% of the pupils chose mango. In pie chart Y, 30% of the pupils chose mango. The number of pupils in each class is not given. Which statement must be true?
options: More pupils in Class A chose mango than in Class B.
Class A has more pupils than Class B.
A greater fraction of the pupils in Class A chose mango than in Class B.
Altogether, 70% of the pupils in the two classes chose mango.
working: A pie chart shows the parts of ONE whole. Without the class sizes, only the fractions of each class can be compared, not the numbers of pupils.
40% is more than 30%, so a greater fraction of Class A chose mango: this must be true.
Watch out: if Class A had 20 pupils and Class B had 40, then 8 pupils in Class A and 12 pupils in Class B chose mango. So 'more pupils in Class A' cannot be told.

distractors.1: Not possible to tell: 40% of a small class can be fewer pupils than 30% of a big class.
distractors.2: Not possible to tell: the pie charts show parts of each class, not how big each class is.
distractors.4: Percentages of two different wholes cannot be added. The combined percentage depends on the class sizes and is between 30% and 40%.

hints: A pie chart shows fractions of one whole. Do you know how big each whole is?
Which statements need the number of pupils in each class? Cross those out.
